:::note[Covers what is coming]
This page also covers a few things that are newer than HotLoop Flow 2.14.1, the latest release. Parts of it may not be in what you have installed. The [release notes](/releases/) say what moved.
:::

HotLoop Flow 2.8.0 adds four things to FlowLab, the diagram tab for test benches and data loggers: analysis nodes, a data acquisition node for NI hardware, an MQTT output that keeps what the broker misses, and a TDMS log. Flows run exactly as they did, a flow file you have today loads and saves byte for byte, and a tab that isn't a diagram doesn't see any of it.

## What's new

**Analysis.** Four nodes work on an array of readings: statistics (mean, RMS, smallest, largest and standard deviation), integral (the area under the array by the trapezoid rule, as one number or as a running area), derivative (the slope at each sample), and a Butterworth filter of order 1 to 10 as a lowpass, highpass, bandpass or bandstop, with the cutoff in hertz.

**A data acquisition node.** `read DAQ task` reads samples from NI hardware, such as a CompactDAQ chassis, through NI's gRPC Device Server. The client is about as small as it can be: Go's own HTTP/2 with hand-written messages, so the binary didn't take on a gRPC library.

**An MQTT output that loses nothing.** `mqtt out` publishes through the broker the flow file configures, the same connection the MQTT nodes use. Mark it durable and a message the broker misses is written to disk before the node finishes and sent, oldest first, when the broker is back, even across a restart. Nothing overtakes anything waiting ahead of it. Its sent output says whether the message went straight out.

**A TDMS log.** `log to TDMS file` appends a record to a TDMS file, one channel per field, and the file opens in the tools a lab already has. A file whose last write was cut short by a power loss still reads up to the last whole value.

## What changed

- There are now 28 node types in the FlowLab section of the palette, up from 21, and the README says so.
- A step that failed once in the 2.7.1 run printed nothing, and the cause was the collector test comparing a span before the log it reads had all of it; it waits for the whole span now. Two more tests were made to wait for what they check. None of that ships.
- The README's pictures were retaken so the top bar says v2.8.0.
- The binary and image sizes in the README were read again for this release.

## New settings

None.

## Upgrade

On amd64, a plain `helm upgrade` to the 2.8.0 image and chart, or the new tag in your Quadlet unit. On arm64, stay where you are until 2.8.1, which is this release with arm64 added and nothing else. Nothing happens on first start and there is nothing to migrate.

Image: `ghcr.io/hotloop-io/hotloop-flow:2.8.0`, linux/amd64 only. We build amd64 first, let it read stable in production, and then one small 2.8.1 with nothing else in it adds arm64. Until then the `2` tag holds the new amd64 image and the arm64 image from 2.7.1, so a box on arm64 that follows `2` or `2.7` keeps what it has, and a box pinned to `2.8.0` needs amd64. Chart: `https://hotloop.io/hotloop-flow/`. The README at this tag has the rest, with pictures: https://github.com/HotLoop-io/hotloop-flow/blob/v2.8.0/README.md
